kinds.task: Runs to completion; show its output and exit code.
kinds.service: Runs until stopped (SIGINT); has a ready signal where one exists.
kinds.stream: Prints continuously until stopped; nothing else depends on it.
kinds.gui: Opens a native window; runs until the window or the process is closed.
kinds.interactive: Needs keyboard input in its own terminal (PTY).
kinds.link: Something to open, not a process.

ros.label: ROS env
ros.description: Inside the platform's ROS 2 environment: Pixi env activated, workspace overlay sourced, ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42, working dir ros2_ws. Pixi task names (build, fmt) also work here.

host.label: Host
host.description: A plain shell on the host machine at the repo root, never inside a container.

host-sudo.label: Host + sudo
host-sudo.description: Host shell at the repo root; prompts for the sudo password, so run it in a terminal (PTY) the user can type into.

link.label: Link
link.description: Not a process: a URL, file or app to open.

platforms.x86-native: x86-64 Linux running the Pixi default env natively, no Docker: every x86 machine without an NVIDIA GPU (set up with x86-cpu), or one whose workspace was built on the host. tooling/host-ros2 strips a system /opt/ros install from the environment first.
platforms.x86-docker: x86-64 Linux + NVIDIA running the billee-desktop image (make setup x86).
platforms.mac: Apple-Silicon Mac running the billee-mac-cpu image. Headless: no RViz window, gamepad, vcan0 or DDS to other machines.
platforms.linux-aarch64: ARM64 Linux, native Pixi env, no container.
platforms.l4t: The Jetson rover, rover-ros2 image. Headless.

needs.display: An X/Wayland display for a window (RViz, Gazebo, rqt). Headless machines put xvfb-run -a in front of sim launches.
needs.vcan0: The virtual CAN interface on the host: run can.vcan-up first (sudo).
needs.can: A real CAN interface (any canN): the Jetson's ODESC bus can2, brought up with can.up, or a USB-CAN adapter.
needs.docker: Docker reachable without sudo (docker info works).
needs.rover: The physical rover. Wheels will turn: put it on blocks first.
needs.terminal: Reads keys from its own terminal: the launcher must give it an interactive PTY.
needs.drivetrain: A running drivetrain item (any of the 'drivetrain' group).
needs.pixi: Pixi on PATH or in ~/.pixi/bin. Machine setup > Set up this machine installs it.
needs.nvidia: An NVIDIA GPU, found on the PCI bus (a Jetson counts).
needs.zed: A ZED 2i on USB. With the ZED SDK (Jetson container) every camera mode works; elsewhere cloud/both use zed_usb (CPU stereo) and OpenPose is skipped. OpenPose also needs its models (Perception > Download OpenPose models) and ~3000 MB free RAM.

blocking.pixi: Pixi isn't installed. Run Machine setup > Set up this machine first.
blocking.nvidia: This machine has no NVIDIA GPU.
blocking.jetson: This machine isn't an NVIDIA Jetson.
blocking.apple-silicon: This machine isn't an Apple-Silicon Mac.

resources.drivetrain: Only one at a time. Each starts /controller_manager, /diff_drive_controller and /robot_state_publisher; two would publish conflicting odometry and TF.
resources.port-8765: foxglove_bridge's WebSocket port. One bridge per machine; a second one fails to bind.
resources.gamepad-nodes: joy_node + joy_tank_drive. The sim starts a pair unless joy_control:=false, teleop.launch.py and ground_station.launch.py start another. Two pairs publish duplicate commands, and an idle pad publishes zeros at 20 Hz.
resources.cmd-vel: /diff_drive_controller/cmd_vel_unstamped. Every publisher here commands the wheels; the controller obeys the last message received.
resources.zed: The ZED 2i. One process can open it: rover.launch.py camera:=..., zed_openpose.launch.py, people_rover.launch.py and zed_usb all do.
resources.pose-estimator: synthetic VIO + EKF + Nav2 servers. The sim starts them unless navigation:=false; a second set would publish a second odom -> base_footprint TF.
